limits: No experiments, data or citations in this chapter; all figures (80%, 100%, 90%, 15%, 30 minutes) are illustrative or asserted.
Case studies are hypothetical and unattributed; outcomes are described, not measured.
Chapter case study 2 outcome text is internally muddled: calls the agent 'Level 4' and also 'a Level 2 implementation (Chapter 12)', mixing the GenAI scale with the implementation scale.
Framework and cloud product names (LangGraph, CrewAI, Cloud Run, Lambda, Agent Engine Memory Bank) will date.
practices: Assess the organization's position on the GenAI Maturity Model before choosing a use case (p.514).
Start with a bounded single-agent (Level 4) use case built on an existing Level 2 RAG foundation, not a multi-agent system (p.514).
Sketch a pattern-first architecture (tools, memory, evaluation, patterns as arrows) before writing code or prompts (p.515, 518).
Give the agent a draft tool but not a submit tool, pause for human approval before irreversible actions (Human-in-the-Loop) (p.510, 515-516).
Wrap flaky tool calls in exponential-backoff Adaptive Retry with a limited retry count (p.510, 517).
Log intermediate reasoning, plans, tool calls and outputs as structured JSON to an immutable store (Instruction Fidelity Auditing, Audit Trail) (p.510, 518, 520).
Before executing, have the agent query context (maintenance schedule) and critique its own plan (Self-Correction) (p.511).
Define auditing, bias detection and compliance processes before deployment; use system-level patterns for multi-agent cascades (p.515-516).
Treat deployment as the start of a continuous improvement loop with AgentOps monitoring (p.516).
Choose the framework from the patterns, not the reverse: state machine (LangGraph) for branching/loops, hierarchical (CrewAI) for delegation (p.513).
Do not attempt a self-improving ecosystem (Implementation Level 3) before mastering grounding and evaluation (GenAI Level 4) (p.512).
Ask for the 'undo' button and blast radius of agent actions; make Human-in-the-Loop non-negotiable for high-stakes actions such as direct deposit changes (p.515, 520).
Containerize, serve via FastAPI/Flask, log, and monitor requests, error rate and latency on a simple cloud service (p.518-519).
